'''Isabel Elaine Allen''' is an American [[Survey methodology|survey statistician]] and [[biostatistics|biostatistician]] who works in [[distance education]], the theory of [[Likert scale]]s, antibacterial treatments, and [[meta-analysis]] of medical trials. She is a professor of biostatistics and [[epidemiology]] at the [[University of California, San Francisco]],{{r|ucsf}} and a professor emeritus of statistics at [[Babson College]].{{r|babson}}

==Education and career==
Allen majored in psychology at [[Skidmore College]], graduating in 1970. She earned a master's degree in mathematics at the [[University of Evansville]] in 1975, and completed her Ph.D. in statistics at [[Cornell University]] in 1979.{{r|penntax}}

She took a faculty position at the [[Wharton School of the University of Pennsylvania]] even before completing her doctorate,{{r|penntax}} and also held faculty positions at the [[Medical College of Pennsylvania]]{{r|skid}} and [[Rutgers University]] prior to her position at [[Babson College]].{{r|babson}} She also taught at [[University of California, San Francisco]].{{r|ucsf}}

As well as her academic work, Allen has helped to found several companies, including the Quahog Research Group, [[ARIAD Pharmaceuticals]],  Pondview Associates, StatSystems, and Bay View Analytics.{{r|skid}}

==Recognition==
Allen was named a [[Fellow of the American Statistical Association]] in 2004.{{r|fasa}} She was the main statistical expert for an [[investigative journalism]] project concerning [[fair housing]], "Long Island Divided",{{r|lid}} which won the 2020 [[Edward R. Murrow Award (Radio Television Digital News Association)|Edward R. Murrow Award]] of the [[Radio Television Digital News Association]] for a news documentary by a large digital news organization.{{r|murrow}}

Skidmore College gave her their Creative Thought Matters Award of Distinction award in 2015.{{r|skid}}
